minutes.headline: PACC reviewed its draft annual town report and FY26 budget plan, and heard the proposed basement studio in the new town hall.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee approved the January 6 and January 20 minutes by roll call, then heard the manager's monthly report and gave proofreading comments on the draft annual town report. It discussed the FY26 budget presentation to the interim town manager, including a possible legal line for a contract renewal, and the proposed studio space in the new town hall extension. The meeting ended with a motion, apparently to adjourn, passed by roll call.

budget_items.what_was_said: The manager gave a total balance as of the monthly report. The captions are garbled and the figure is repeated several times differently. He said nothing remarkable and no interest had been earned in a couple of months.
The manager worked on the budget with Steve Walker and presented it to the interim town manager for review.

The legal line has no money in it. The contract expires in 2028 and renewal talks usually start two years early, which could fall in FY26. The plan is to raise the issue now and put money in at a special town meeting.
Capital now has to come out of the enterprise fund directly because of reduced contest income.
Interest on the investments is missing from the FY24 revenue and expenses in the report. The manager was asked to add it, and a member wanted a statement confirming the investment.
The select board is to see a first cost estimate with a target. The estimate is based on a per-square-foot new-construction figure. There was concern the basement is not priced like the upstairs.
The financials show the rent payment was finally taken in December. Members joked about what rent a new location might charge, and said the committee is a town department and should not pay.
The treasurer may get more freedom for risk-free investments such as bonds. Members said the committee should pay attention if it earns more.

decisions.decision: The program submission policy stays on the agenda and is tabled for now, still waiting on the town attorney's review.
The master plan steering committee update item is to be removed from future agendas. The committee failed to reach a quorum.
Report comments go only to the manager, who will make the edits and hope to send the report by February 14. Others should reply all.
A member will contact the municipal building design committee that evening to get the equipment room access fixed.
The manager's phone and email contacts for possible alternate studio spaces will be kept on file. No outreach was agreed.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed that the master plan steering committee update will be removed from future agendas, after that committee failed to reach a quorum.
The committee tabled the program submission policy again; it is still waiting on the town attorney's review.
The manager said the FY26 budget has no money in the legal line, though the contract expires in 2028 and renewal talks could fall in FY26; the plan is to raise it at a special town meeting.
Members asked that interest on investments, missing from the FY24 revenue and expenses, be added to the draft annual town report; comments go only to the manager.
The committee approved the January 6 and January 20 minutes by roll call, and heard an update on studio space in the new town hall.

why_it_matters: The cable committee's budget is paid from an enterprise fund, and capital now has to come from that fund directly because of reduced contest income, so less money is available for equipment and studio costs.

The committee's studio space in the new town hall depends on a cost estimate that members worry prices the basement like the upstairs, and an unfunded legal line could mean a request at a special town meeting.
